cover_letter.subject: Application for the Quantitative Research Intern position – Gas & Electricity Market-Making Team (GBU Supply & Energy Management) – 6-month internship, 1 March to 31 August 2027
paragraphs: I am writing to apply for the Quantitative Research Intern position within the Gas & Electricity Market-Making Team of ENGIE's GBU Supply & Energy Management. I am currently completing a double degree: an MSc in Applied Mathematics & Statistics – Quantitative Finance & Actuarial Science at the University of Bordeaux, together with an engineering degree in Computer Science, Data & AI at ENSEIRB-MATMECA (Bordeaux INP). I am looking for a 6-month end-of-studies internship from 1 March to 31 August 2027, and research on how weather shapes short-term power markets is exactly where I want to apply statistics and machine learning.

My coursework covers probability, stochastic calculus, Monte Carlo methods, regression and machine learning, including deep learning. To work directly on the problems described in your posting, I carried out a Weather Forecast Verification & Aggregation project in Python (xarray, pandas): I aligned ECMWF and GFS forecast runs from open data, assessed them with bias, RMSE and CRPS by lead time, and built a skill-weighted blend. This is close to your missions of assessing the accuracy of forecast runs and combining sources into aggregated datasets that better isolate the weather signal.

My internships taught me to be rigorous with data. At Inside Therapeutics, as a Quantitative Data Analysis & Automation Intern, I designed and built LabData on my own, a Python / PostgreSQL / Streamlit platform that went into production in 7 weeks, processing around 500 samples per month with independent validation of calculations, reconciliation and an audit trail (4,123 tests, 91% coverage). On my own initiative I added an analysis layer (correlations, trend regressions, measurement noise versus process variability, anomaly alerts) and prototyped a Gaussian-process model on a design of experiments with uncertainty-guided active learning. At Société Générale, as a Data Analyst Intern – Capital Markets, I integrated 6 data sources in Python and SQL into automated, controlled flows feeding P&L tools, and replaced manual checks with more than 25 automated data-quality and compliance controls reported in Power BI to Finance, Risk and Trading teams.

Presenting technical results clearly matters to me: I presented LabData to the management committee and launched and ran an internal AI workshop. I would welcome the opportunity to work alongside your traders, turn weather research into useful market insights and discuss my application with you in an interview.
